title: Human-review approval record
description: Every human gate in this project records its verdict here. Three amendments in a row produced the same defect — a release gate blocking on a gitignored path (.omc/state/…), which works on the author's laptop and fails on the first CI clone. AC-X.7a closes it: every human-review artifact lives under tracked .approvals/, is schema-validated, and is bound to BOTH the deployment URL and the commit SHA it approves. Approving a preview and shipping something else must not be expressible.

reviewer.description: The human who reviewed. A name, not a role — roles cannot be asked follow-up questions.

timestamp.description: ISO-8601, UTC. Commits touching the approved surface must post-date this; an approval that predates the work it approves approves nothing.

deployment_url.description: The exact URL the reviewer looked at. Not localhost — fonts render differently, and half of what these gates judge is type.

commit_sha.description: Full 40-character SHA of the commit deployed at deployment_url.

notes.description: Free text. Required when the verdict is not a clean approval.

evidence.description: Typed evidence binding the verdict to the artifact it judged, so that approving one thing and shipping another fails the gate rather than passing it quietly.

scale_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the type-scale block in src/styles.css, as it stood when approved. g1.sh re-computes and compares it at release. Required for the typography gate.

specimen_url.description: The deployed type-specimen route the reviewer compared against.

screenshots.description: Paths, repo-relative, to any screenshots taken at review time.

reviewed_paths.description: Repo-relative paths the reviewer was asked to judge. A later commit touching one of these without a fresh approval is a gate failure, not a warning.
